arithmetic_proof.full_domain_reasoning: Let A=2^(32+k), e=m*d-A>0, and x be the signed bit interpretation of wrapped(end-first). Native q0=floor(m*x/A), then q=q0+(q0<0). For 0<=x<=2^31-1, e*x<A, so writing x=d*n+r gives n<=m*x/A<n+1, hence q=n. For -2^31<=x<0, write y=-x=d*n+r. With e*y<A the strictly positive error <1/d gives n<m*y/A<n+1, hence q0=-n-1 and sign correction returns -n (including r=0). For d24 the sole equality e*y=A is y=2^31; r=8, not d-1, so the same bound still gives ceil=n+1. Direct integer form at this endpoint q0=floor(-0x2aaaaaab/8)=-89478486 and q=-89478485, matching trunc(-2147483648/24). No divide-by-zero or MIN/-1 case exists. C++17 uint32 subtraction plus memcpy int32 bit transfer followed by /positive constant implements exactly this quotient without pointer subtraction, signed subtraction overflow, out-of-range unsigned-to-signed cast or guessed valid-range narrowing.
arithmetic_proof.whole_code_evidence: All complete measured C++17 strict and actual registered sections equal the corresponding whole Native bodies, including load schedule, branch, volatile outputs, flags, fault prefixes and plain RET; no helper section was omitted.
